title: Material pressure is jointly distributed across work limitation, children, and resources
source_unit: SIPP person record by reference month, stratified by released work-limiting-condition status, household members under 18, and monthly household income-to-poverty ratio

observations.period: 2024 reference year; work-limiting condition, no household members under 18, below 1.00x poverty

denominator.unit: valid person-month records for utility and job measures; outcome-specific food universes differ

observations.method: Official SIPP status flags and outcome universes; WPFINWGT full estimate with 240 Fay-BRR replicate weights, G=240, perturbation factor 0.5.
observations.uncertainty: Person-weighted descriptive cell; food outcomes have separate valid universes. Household outcomes repeat across people and are not household-weighted.
observations.subgroup: EDISABL indicates a condition limiting the kind or amount of work; RHNUMU18 indicates one or more household members under 18; THINCPOV is monthly household income-to-poverty ratio.
observations.counterinterpretation: Children-in-household status is not parenthood or care hours; work limitation is not a complete disability measure; low-resource and high-pressure cells bundle housing, health, age, family, and labor-market composition.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; no work-limiting condition, one or more household members under 18, below 1.00x poverty

denominator.unit: valid person-month records for utility and job measures; outcome-specific food universes differ

observations.method: Same official-universe and Fay-BRR method as the work-limiting-condition cell.
observations.uncertainty: Reference comparison is descriptive and not a counterfactual; person-weighted and outcome-specific universes remain in force.
observations.subgroup: No released work-limiting condition; one or more household members under 18; below 1.00x monthly income-to-poverty ratio.
observations.counterinterpretation: The comparison does not isolate children, disability, income, or work status; family composition, age, housing, care, and employment mix may account for differences.

observations.period: 2024 reference year; work-limiting condition, one or more household members under 18, 4.00x poverty or more

denominator.unit: valid person-month records for utility and job measures; hunger universe has 368 valid records

observations.method: Same official-universe and Fay-BRR method as the low-resource cells.
observations.uncertainty: The high-resource child-present work-limiting hunger cell is sparse and highly imprecise; its point estimate must not be ranked as a stable pattern.
observations.subgroup: Work-limiting condition; one or more household members under 18; 4.00x monthly income-to-poverty ratio or more.
observations.counterinterpretation: The lower hunger point estimate than the child-absent high-resource work-limiting cell is a counter-pattern with a 10.41-point SE, not evidence that children protect food security.

related_sources.claim: Official work-limitation, household-composition, outcome status flags, and universe definitions.

boundary: This is a person-weighted, design-based intersectional distribution. It does not establish household prevalence, care hours, parenthood, causal effects, a dated bill or employer event, accommodation, recovery, trust, political action, or firm/state response.
